CDISC datasets

Source: vignettes/articles/cdisc.Rmd
cdisc.Rmd

sideview recognises tables that look like SDTM, SEND or ADaM datasets and marks them with a badge. This is for awareness: it helps you see what each card is. It does not check a dataset against an implementation guide, and a table that does not look like CDISC data is left alone.

Everything below uses a small synthetic study built in the page (no real patients).

A synthetic study 

usub <- paste0("SV-001-", sprintf("%03d", 1:4))
sid <- "SV-001"

dm <- data.frame(STUDYID = sid, DOMAIN = "DM", USUBJID = usub, SUBJID = sprintf("%03d", 1:4),
                 AGE = c(34, 51, 62, 45), SEX = c("F", "M", "F", "M"),
                 ARM = c("A", "B", "A", "B"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
attr(dm$USUBJID, "label") <- "Unique Subject Identifier"
attr(dm$AGE, "label") <- "Age"
attr(dm, "label") <- "Demographics"

ae <- data.frame(STUDYID = sid, DOMAIN = "AE", USUBJID = usub, AESEQ = 1:4,
                 AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Rash", "Cough"),
                 AESEV = c("MILD", "MODERATE", "MILD", "SEVERE"),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

suppae <- data.frame(STUDYID = sid, RDOMAIN = "AE", USUBJID = usub, IDVAR = "AESEQ",
                     IDVARVAL = as.character(1:4), QNAM = "AETRTEM",
                     QLABEL = "Treatment Emergent", QVAL = "Y", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

adsl <- data.frame(STUDYID = sid, USUBJID = usub, TRT01P = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
                   TRT01A = c("A", "B", "A", "B"), AGE = dm$AGE, SAFFL = "Y",
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

Badges 

sideview_widget(dm = dm, ae = ae, suppae = suppae, adsl = adsl)

Each recognised card gets a badge after its name: DM, AE, SUPPAE and ADSL here. Hover over a badge for the dataset label, the standard and class, and the evidence used (for example “DOMAIN column = DM” or “STUDYID + USUBJID”). SUPPAE also says which parent it supplements. Column headers show a variable’s label as a tooltip, L shows a row of labels under the headers (it is saved with the workspace), and Ctrl+K finds a card by its domain or dataset label.

The tags are worked out in R when the canvas is built. They are never saved in a workspace file; they are worked out again when it is opened.

Overrides with cdisc =

cdisc is "auto" by default. Turn it off with FALSE, or name the domain of a table that sideview cannot tell on its own:

sideview_widget(my_events = ae, cdisc = FALSE)
sideview_widget(my_events = ae[, -2], cdisc = c(my_events = "AE"))

The same argument is on sideview(), save_sideview(), sideviewServer() and sv_codebook(). In a Shiny module the badges follow sv_add_card() and sv_replace_card().

Domains in the codebook

sv_codebook() gets a domain column, and the widget’s CSV download matches it.

cb <- sv_codebook(dm = dm, ae = ae, adsl = adsl)
unique(cb[, c("table", "domain")])
#>    table domain
#> 1     dm     DM
#> 8     ae     AE
#> 14  adsl   ADSL

With cdisc = FALSE the column is NA.

The catalogue 

cat <- sv_cdisc_catalogue()
head(cat[, 1:min(5, ncol(cat))])
#>   name                      label           class standard ig_versions
#> 1   DM               Demographics Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 2   CO                   Comments Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 3   SE           Subject Elements Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 4   SV             Subject Visits Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 5   SM Subject Disease Milestones Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 6   AG           Procedure Agents   Interventions     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4

The catalogue lists the datasets sideview knows. Its ig_versions column (implementation guide versions) is approximate. It exists so badges can say what a table is, not to validate it.

Reading CDISC files

sv_read_cdisc() reads a folder, or a set of files, of .xpt, .sas7bdat, Dataset-JSON (.json) and .parquet into a named list, keeping variable labels. Names are the lower-case file stems. It needs the package for each format (haven, datasetjson, arrow), and it never uses the network.

study <- sv_read_cdisc("study/sdtm")
sideview_widget(study)

Parquet files stay on disk as Arrow Datasets unless you pass lazy = FALSE.

What it does not do

  • The ig_versions in the catalogue are approximate, and nothing is validated against an implementation guide.
  • For a name that is not in the catalogue, the variable prefix (for example AE...) wins over ADaM structure, so an ADAE-like table may be tagged as an SDTM AE domain.
  • cdisc = FALSE shows no tags, but lazy (arrow / duckdb) cards still run detection when they are built. A named cdisc = vector with several lazy cards gets slower with each verb.
  • Dataset-JSON reading was not tested against the real datasetjson package; if its structure differs, the file is skipped with a warning.
  • The Copilot gets column labels and a domain line as schema text, never row data.
  • The label row is placed from one measurement of the header height, so it could sit off if a header grows taller later.
  • The interface was checked in headless Chrome, not in RStudio’s dialog or Viewer pane.
